blitzmax.trace.server.description: Traces the communication between VS Code and the BlitzMax language server.

blitzmax.base.path.markdownDescription: Absolute path to the BlitzMax SDK root. You can override this in a workspace's `.vscode/settings.json`, or separately in each folder of a multi-root workspace. Builds use the SDK of the source file's folder. To run a language server from each folder's SDK, also enable #blitzmax.lsp.multi# and reload VS Code.

blitzmax.pref.showProblemsOnBuildError.description: Display the problems view on build task errors.

blitzmax.pref.jumpToProblemOnBuildError.description: Jump to the first problem on build task errors.

blitzmax.pref.showBuildProgress.description: Show build progress notification for build tasks.

blitzmax.lsp.path.markdownDescription: Relative or absolute path to the language server. A relative path starts at #blitzmax.base.path#, so the default finds the `bls` that ships inside BlitzMax NG.

blitzmax.lsp.multi.markdownDescription: Run a separate language server for each workspace folder. Enable this when folders use different BlitzMax SDKs or LSP executables: each folder resolves #blitzmax.base.path# and #blitzmax.lsp.path# independently, while folders without overrides use your default settings. When disabled, one language server handles all BlitzMax files using the global SDK and LSP paths.

blitzmax.lsp.args.markdownDescription: Arguments to start the language server with. `bls` takes none, so this is here for a different server.

blitzmax.lsp.hotReload.markdownDescription:
Restart the language server when its binary changes on disk, for when you are building the server yourself.  
*(only supported on Linux and macOS)*

enumDescriptions: Follow the default BlitzMax build task.
Read the project the way a release build sees it.
Read the project the way a debug build sees it, so `?Debug` code counts.
blitzmax.lsp.buildMode.markdownDescription: Which build the language server reads your project as. Empty follows the default build task. It decides which module interfaces get loaded and which `?Debug` code is live.

blitzmax.lsp.targetPlatform.markdownDescription: The platform the language server reads your project for. Empty follows the default BlitzMax build task. Set an override and that target's conditional symbols go live, so `?Win32` code gets checked while you work on Linux.

blitzmax.lsp.targetArchitecture.markdownDescription: The architecture the language server reads your project for. Empty follows the default BlitzMax build task. Not every architecture goes with every #blitzmax.lsp.targetPlatform#.

blitzmax.lsp.conditionalSymbols.markdownDescription: The whole set of conditional symbols to hold true. Leave it empty and the target picks its own, which is what you want nearly always. Filling it in replaces that set rather than adding to it, so name the platform, the architecture and `threaded` yourself.

blitzmax.lsp.requireCoreInterface.markdownDescription: Wait for the core module interfaces to be readable before analysing. Turning it off lets the server answer from an incomplete picture, so it starts missing things a build would catch.

blitzmax.lsp.useDependencySnapshots.markdownDescription: Read imported modules from the interface files a build left behind instead of parsing their source every time. Off is much slower, and only worth it while you are editing a module itself.

blitzmax.lsp.warnImplicitDefaultReturns.markdownDescription: Warn about a function that runs off its end without a `Return` and so hands back the default for its type.

blitzmax.help.customStyle.description: Use custom CSS style for help documentation.

blitzmax.format.indent.markdownDescription: Indent parsed block bodies using the editor's tab size and spaces-or-tabs setting. Example: `Function Show()` ↵ `Print value` becomes `Function Show()` ↵ `····Print value` (each `·` represents a space). Comments, directives, multiline text, and continuation lines keep their existing indentation.

blitzmax.format.trimTrailingWhitespace.markdownDescription: Remove spaces and tabs at the ends of ordinary code and single-line comment lines. Example: `Print value··` → `Print value` (each `·` represents a space). Multiline strings, block comments, directives, pragmas, and native lines retain their contents.

blitzmax.format.spaceAfterComma.markdownDescription: Use one space after commas when the next code token is on the same line. Example: `Draw(x,y)` → `Draw(x, y)`. When disabled, existing comma spacing is preserved. Wrapped lists, comments, and multiline strings keep their layout.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Lines from top to bottom: `Select n` ↵ `····Case 1` ↵ `········Print n` (each `·` represents a space).
Lines from top to bottom: `Select n` ↵ `Case 1` ↵ `····Print n` (each `·` represents a space).
blitzmax.format.caseIndent.markdownDescription: Indent `Case` and `Default` under `Select`, or align them with `Select`. Statements in each case remain one level deeper than the case label.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Keep existing spacing: `{nomangle}` stays `{nomangle}`; `{ nomangle }` stays `{ nomangle }`.
Add one space inside single-line metadata braces: `{nomangle}` → `{ nomangle }`.
Remove optional spaces inside single-line metadata braces: `{ nomangle }` → `{nomangle}`.
blitzmax.format.metadataBraceSpacing.markdownDescription: Spacing inside single-line metadata braces: `{ nomangle }` or `{nomangle}`. Empty and multiline braces retain their layout.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Keep existing spacing: `Call(value)` stays `Call(value)`; `Call( value )` stays `Call( value )`.
Add one space inside single-line call parentheses: `Call(value)` → `Call( value )`.
Remove optional spaces inside single-line call parentheses: `Call( value )` → `Call(value)`.
blitzmax.format.callParenSpacing.markdownDescription: Spacing inside single-line call and constructor parentheses: `Call( value )` or `Call(value)`. Declarations and wrapped calls retain their layout.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Keep existing spacing around assignments: `value=1` stays `value=1`.
Add one space on each side: `value=1` → `value = 1`.
Remove optional spaces: `value = 1` → `value=1`, where this keeps the same tokens.
blitzmax.format.assignmentSpacing.markdownDescription: Preserve spacing, use one space, or remove spaces around parsed assignments and initializers. Compact spacing is used only when adjacent tokens remain unchanged.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Keep existing spacing around binary operators: `a+b` stays `a+b`.
Add one space on each side: `a+b` → `a + b`.
Remove optional spaces: `a + b` → `a+b`. Word operators such as `And` keep required spaces.
blitzmax.format.binarySpacing.markdownDescription: Preserve spacing, use one space, or remove spaces around parsed binary operators. Word operators such as `And` keep the spaces needed to remain separate tokens. Unary operators and type syntax retain their layout.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Keep the current header: `If ready` and `If ready Then` stay as written.
Add `Then` to multiline headers: `If ready` → `If ready Then`.
Remove `Then` from multiline headers: `If ready Then` → `If ready`.
blitzmax.format.thenStyle.markdownDescription: How to write `Then` in multiline `If` and `ElseIf` headers. Inline statements keep their existing `Then`.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Keep the current ending: `EndFunction` and `End Function` stay as written.
Combine named endings: `End Function` → `EndFunction`.
Separate named endings: `EndFunction` → `End Function`.
blitzmax.format.endStyle.markdownDescription: How to write named block endings, such as `EndFunction` or `End Function`.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Keep simple one-line statements such as `If ready Then Print value` on one line.
Split `If ready Then Print value` into three lines: `If ready Then` ↵ `····Print value` ↵ `End If` (each `·` represents a space).
blitzmax.format.inlineIfStyle.markdownDescription: Expand simple one-statement inline `If` statements into a multiline block. Inline statements with `Else`, comments, or other code on the line remain unchanged.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Keep existing blank lines after declarations.
Use one blank line between a completed declaration and the next statement: `End Method` ↵ *(blank line)* ↵ `Method Next()`.
Use no blank line between a completed declaration and the next statement: `End Method` ↵ `Method Next()`.
blitzmax.format.declarationBlankLines.markdownDescription: Blank lines after completed functions, methods, types, enums and extern blocks when another statement follows at the same level. Gaps containing comments or directives are preserved.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Keep existing blank lines after control blocks.
Use one blank line after a completed control block when a sibling statement follows: `End If` ↵ *(blank line)* ↵ `Print result`.
Use no blank line after a completed control block when a sibling statement follows: `End If` ↵ `Print result`.
blitzmax.format.controlBlankLines.markdownDescription: Blank lines after `End If`, `Next`, `Wend`, `Until`/`Forever`, `End Select`, and similar completed control blocks. Nested closing lines and gaps containing comments or directives are preserved.

blitzmax.formatter.path.markdownDescription: Relative or absolute path to the code formatter. A relative path starts at #blitzmax.base.path#, so the default finds a `bfm` dropped into BlitzMax NG's `bin` folder.

blitzmax.formatter.onType.markdownDescription: [Code formatter](https://github.com/search?q=topic%3ABlitzMax+topic%3Aformatter) arguments when using VS Code option `Format On Type`.

blitzmax.formatter.useRange.markdownDescription: Use range arguments instead of sending text selection when [formatting code](https://github.com/search?q=topic%3ABlitzMax+topic%3Aformatter).

blitzmax.formatter.range.start.markdownDescription: [Code formatter](https://github.com/search?q=topic%3ABlitzMax+topic%3Aformatter) arguments for start of format range.

blitzmax.formatter.range.end.markdownDescription: [Code formatter](https://github.com/search?q=topic%3ABlitzMax+topic%3Aformatter) arguments for end of format range.

blitzmax.formatter.file.markdownDescription: Argument used to tell the code formatter which file the text came from. A formatter reading standard input cannot otherwise find a settings file sitting next to your source, so this is what makes per folder formatting settings work. Leave it empty for a formatter that does not take one.

blitzmax.syntax.colorFunctions.description: An array of all the functions that sets a color

viewsWelcome.contents:
Open a BlitzMax file or folder to edit your BlitzMax build options here.
[Open File](command:workbench.action.files.openFile)
[Open Folder](command:vscode.openFolder)
To learn more about BlitzMax NG [visit our homepage](https://blitzmax.org/).
Set your BlitMax path and make sure module documentation are built.

markdownEnumDescriptions:
Builds an applicatio from a single root source file  
`bmk makeapp)`  
[More info](https://blitzmax.org/docs/en/tools/bmk/#makeapp)

Builds a set of modules  
`bmk makemods)`  
[More info](https://blitzmax.org/docs/en/tools/bmk/#makemods)

On Win3, builds a dynamic linked library (DLL) from the source file  
`bmk makelib)`  
[More info](https://blitzmax.org/docs/en/tools/bmk/#makelib)

Builds a bootstrap package  
`bmk makebootstrap`  
[More info](https://blitzmax.org/docs/en/tools/bmk/#makebootstrap)

onlycompile.markdownDescription:
Compile sources only, no building of the application  
`bmk compile`  
[More info](https://blitzmax.org/docs/en/tools/bmk/#compile)

source.markdownDescription:
Build root source file. Use `${file}` to build the active editor file, or choose a `.bmx` file to lock builds to that application root.  
`bmk <source>`  
[More info](https://blitzmax.org/docs/en/tools/bmk/#command-line-syntax)

fullcompile.markdownDescription:
Recompiles all source/modules regardless of timestamp  
`bmk -a`  
[More info](https://blitzmax.org/docs/en/tools/bmk/#-a)

appstub.markdownDescription:
Builds an app using a custom appstub  
`bmk -b <custom appstub module>`  
[More info](https://blitzmax.org/docs/en/tools/bmk/#-b-custom-appstub-module)

hidpi.markdownDescription:
Specifies that the application supports high-resolution screens  
`bmk -hi`

gdb.markdownDescription:
Generates line mappings suitable for GDB debugging  
`bmk -gdb`  
[More info](https://blitzmax.org/docs/en/tools/bmk/#-gdb)

gprof.markdownDescription:
Gprof is a performance analysis tool for Unix applications  
`bmk -gprof`

universal.markdownDescription:
Creates a Universal build for supported platforms (Mac OS X and iOS)  
`bmk -i`  
[More info](https://blitzmax.org/docs/en/tools/bmk/#-i)

target.markdownDescription:
Cross-compiles to the specific target platform  
`bmk -l <target-platform>`  
[More info](https://blitzmax.org/docs/en/tools/bmk/#-l-target-platform)

picoHeap.markdownDescription:
Pico managed heap size (`auto` or a sized value)  
`bmk -heap <auto|size>`

picoStorage.markdownDescription:
Reserved persistent Pico flash storage (`none` or a sector-aligned size)  
`bmk -storage <none|size>`

picoUpload.markdownDescription:
Upload and start the Pico UF2 with picotool after building  
`bmk -x`

esp32Upload.description: Upload and start the ESP32 firmware after building (bmk -x).

musl.markdownDescription:
Enables musl libc compatibility (Linux NG only)  
`bmk -musl`  
[More info](https://blitzmax.org/docs/en/tools/bmk/#-musl)

nostrictupgrade.markdownDescription:
Don't upgrade strict method void return types, if required  
`bmk -nostrictupgrade`  
[More info](https://blitzmax.org/docs/en/tools/bmk/#-nostrictupgrade)

output.markdownDescription:
Specifies the output file relative to the workspace foder  
`bmk -o <output-file>`  
[More info](https://blitzmax.org/docs/en/tools/bmk/#-o-output-file)

quick.markdownDescription:
Do not scan modules for changes  
`bmk -quick`  
[More info](https://blitzmax.org/docs/en/tools/bmk/#-quick)

standalone.markdownDescription:
Generate but do not compile into binary form  
`bmk -standalone`  
[More info](https://blitzmax.org/docs/en/tools/bmk/#-standalone)

markdownEnumDescriptions: Shows error
Shows warning
funcargcasting.markdownDescription:
How to handle function argument casting issues  
`bmk -w`  
[More info](https://blitzmax.org/docs/en/tools/bmk/#-w)

framework.markdownDescription:
Defines to use a specific module as framework  
`bmk -f <framework>`  
[More info](https://blitzmax.org/docs/en/tools/bmk/#-f-framework)

nomanifest.markdownDescription:
Do not generate a manifest file for the built application  
`bmk -nomanifest`  
[More info](https://blitzmax.org/docs/en/tools/bmk/#-nomanifest)

single.markdownDescription:
Disabled multi threaded processing in a bmk built with thread support  
`bmk -single`  
[More info](https://blitzmax.org/docs/en/tools/bmk/#-single)

nodef.markdownDescription:
Do not generate .def files useable by created DLLs/shared libraries  
`bmk -nodef`  
[More info](https://blitzmax.org/docs/en/tools/bmk/#-nodef)

nohead.markdownDescription:
Do not generate header files useable by created DLLs/shared libraries  
`bmk -nohead`  
[More info](https://blitzmax.org/docs/en/tools/bmk/#-nohead)

override.markdownDescription:
Sets requirement for overriding methods and functions to append override to their definitions  
`bmk -override`  
[More info](https://blitzmax.org/docs/en/tools/bmk/#-override)

overerr.markdownDescription:
Defines missing override keywords in overridden methods and functions to be handled as error instead of warning  
`bmk -overerr`  
[More info](https://blitzmax.org/docs/en/tools/bmk/#-overerr)

nopie.markdownDescription:
Do not generate PIE binaries (Linux only)  
`bmk -no-pie`  
[More info](https://blitzmax.org/docs/en/tools/bmk/#-no-pie)

upx.markdownDescription:
Compress the created binary with UPX  
`bmk -upx`  
[More info](https://blitzmax.org/docs/en/tools/bmk/#-upx)
